name: Ano Nuevo SP
description: Año Nuevo State Park on the San Mateo coast is home to one of the world's largest mainland breeding colonies of northern elephant seals, with a Marine Education Center and coastal trails.
fullDescription: Año Nuevo State Park on the San Mateo coast is home to one of the world's largest mainland breeding colonies of northern elephant seals, with a Marine Education Center and coastal trails.
whatTheyOffer:
- Elephant seal viewing: self-guided from April to November with a free Visitor Permit (issued 8:30 am-3:30 pm at the entrance)
- Docent-led guided seal walks required during breeding season (mid-December through March), reserved through ReserveCalifornia.com; the viewing area is closed December 1-14
- Equal Access Tours for visitors needing mobility assistance (phone reservations)
- Marine Education Center with natural history exhibits
- Day use only (no camping); no pets allowed
- Open 8:30 am to sunset; phone (650) 879-2025
howToGetIt:
**Fees:**
- Day use: $10 per vehicle ($9 with a senior 62+)
- Guided seal walks require a reservation during breeding season

**Save with park passes:** Año Nuevo accepts the California Explorer, Golden Poppy, Disabled Discount, Distinguished Veteran, Golden Bear, and Senior Golden Bear passes, plus the California State Library Parks Pass (free to check out at public libraries).
address: 1 New Years Creek Road & Hwy 1, Pescadero, CA, 94060
keywords: Ano Nuevo, state park, Pescadero, elephant seals, wildlife, coastal, hiking, guided tours, nature reserve
